subject: the 40k mistake we almost made
preheader: a nashville duplex, a dscr of 1.08, and a better deal next door.
headline: How TrueCap caught a $40,000 mistake on a Nashville duplex.
body: An investor I know was about to close on a duplex in East Nashville. $385,000, $1,650 per unit, $3,300/mo gross. He'd run the cap rate (looked like 6.2%), liked the location, and was three days from inspection contingency.

He ran the address through TrueCap on a Saturday morning, mostly to grab a PDF for his lender. The verdict came back Mixed with a DSCR of 1.08. Below his lender's 1.20 floor. He didn't believe it — ran the numbers in his own spreadsheet. Same answer.

What had he missed? Property tax. Davidson County had reassessed the area last year and the new assessment was 22% higher than what the seller's prior bill reflected. He'd modeled the seller's old tax bill (about $3,800) instead of the new one (about $4,900). $1,100 of NOI he didn't have. DSCR collapsed.

He killed the deal. Two weeks later he closed on a smaller duplex three blocks over at $310,000 with $1,500 per unit and a clean DSCR of 1.31. Roughly $40,000 less price, better cash flow, loan got approved without a rate bump.
The point isn't 'TrueCap is magic.' The point is that one bad assumption (old tax bill instead of reassessed value) was about to cost him $40,000. Sixty seconds caught it.
